title: UTEP fires head football coach Scotty Walden
content:
UTEP has fired coach Scotty Walden near the end of his third season, opening one of the toughest jobs in FBS.

Walden went 6-28 and never won more than three games in any season. The Miners are 1-9 this season. Walden arrived at UTEP after a 26-14 run at FCS Austin Peay.

“We are grateful to Scotty for the countless hours he’s put in leading our program,” athletic director Jim Senter said in a statement. “His tenure has been marked by unprecedented success in recruiting and record-breaking team academic performance. He has excelled at community relations and fundraising, and has put his own money back into the program. We haven’t seen the necessary improvement from year one to year three and believe it’s time for new leadership. We wish Scotty well in his future endeavors.”

UTEP, which joined the Mountain West from Conference USA this year, has just two winning seasons in the past 20 years. It hasn’t won more than eight games in a season since 1988 and has just six bowl appearances since 1989.

Walden did improve the roster during his tenure. The Miners are second in the Mountain West in 247Sports’ Team Talent composite ratings, which are based on the high school ratings of players. But while the program is in Texas, its isolated location at the western tip of the state on the Mexico border is far from the fertile recruiting areas. El Paso is closer to the border of California than it is to Dallas. Still, the vast majority of Walden’s roster was made up of Texas players.

Walden was one of the lowest-paid head coaches in FBS, with an $800,000 annual salary, which will limit the pool of potential candidates. The buyout owed to him is $1 million, subject to offset from what Walden earns from his next coaching job.

Potential names to watch for the UTEP job include Texas Tech offensive coordinator Mack Leftwich (a former UTEP player), Lamar coach Pete Rossomando, Prairie View A&M coach Tremaine Jackson, Stephen F. Austin coach Colby Carthel, Tarleton State coach Todd Whitten, Texas Tech running backs and associate head coach Kenny Perry and former Florida State defensive coordinator Tony White (who went to high school in El Paso).
